nodes.title: Adic morphisms and the four finite-type classes
nodes.statement: For a morphism of adic spaces f: X -> Y, define: f adic (locally, O_Y(V) -> O_X(U) is an adic ring homomorphism; equivalently f(X_a) ⊆ Y_a; automatic when Y is analytic); f locally of weakly finite type (the ring map O_Y(V) -> O_X(U) of f-adic rings is of topologically finite type); locally of +weakly finite type (additionally O_X^+(U) is the integral closure of O_Y^+(V)[E ∪ O_X(U)^{oo}] for a finite set E); locally of finite type (the map of affinoid rings (O_Y(V),O_Y^+(V)) -> (O_X(U),O_X^+(U)) is of topologically finite type); locally of finite presentation (finite type, plus finite presentation of the ring map when O_Y(V) is discrete). Each class is stable under restriction to open subspaces and under composition, and the classes are nested: finite presentation ⊆ finite type ⊆ +weakly finite type ⊆ weakly finite type ⊆ adic. For affinoid X -> Y of finite type the affinoid ring map is itself of topologically finite type. For rigid varieties, r(f) is locally of finite type.
hypotheses: Adic spaces in Huber's sense (structure sheaf of complete f-adic rings with valuations); affinoid rings (A^▷, A^+)
The notions 'adic' and 'of topologically finite type' for ring homomorphisms are those of Huber 1994 [Hu, §3]; that paper is not in the library
proofSteps: Define each class locally on affinoid opens as in Definition 1.2.1 and record the inclusions displayed after it.
Independence of the chosen affinoid opens is quoted from [Hu, 3.2] and [Hu4, 3.3.23, 3.8.15]; those proofs were not read.
acceptance: Every morphism to an analytic adic space is adic.
For a rigid morphism f, r(f) is locally of finite type; if f is a morphism of affinoid rigid varieties the affinoid ring map is of topologically finite type.

nodes.title: Existence of fibre products of adic spaces (Huber 1.2.2) and their stability properties
nodes.statement: Let f: X -> Z and g: Y -> Z be morphisms of adic spaces. The fibre product X ×_Z Y exists in the category of adic spaces if (a) f is locally of finite type, or (b) f is locally of weakly finite type and g is adic. In case (b) with X, Y, Z affinoid the fibre product is Spa of the affinoid ring D = (D^▷, D^+) with D^▷ = C^▷ ⊗_{A^▷} B^▷ topologised by {I^n D_0}, D_0 the image of C_0 ⊗_{A_0} B_0 and D^+ the integral closure of C^+ ⊗_{A^+} B^+ in D^▷; the square of affinoid rings is cocartesian. In case (a) with C = A⟨T⟩_M/I, the fibre product is the increasing union of the affinoid spaces W_m = Spa B⟨T⟩_{φ(M) ∪ L^m}/J_m (L a finite set of topologically nilpotent elements of B with (φ(M_i) ∪ L^m)·B^▷ open), each W_{m_1} -> W_{m_2} being an open embedding onto the rational subset {v(ℓT_i) ≤ 1}. Consequences (Corollary 1.2.3): base change preserves locally finite presentation / finite type (case a), +weakly finite type (case b), weakly finite type and adicity, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of the base-changed leg, and points of X ×_Z Y surject onto pairs (x,t) with f(x) = g(t).
hypotheses: Case (a): f locally of finite type; case (b): f locally of weakly finite type and g adic
Continuous extension of maps on A⟨T⟩_M uses the universal property [Hu, 3.5] of restricted power series over f-adic rings (unread)
Sheafiness of the affinoid rings D, B⟨T⟩/J_m is not discussed at this point of the source; Huber's adic spaces are assumed to have sheafy affinoid pieces where they are defined
proofSteps: Case (b): form the tensor product of the underlying rings, the ring of definition D_0 with the I-adic topology, D^+ as integral closure; check the cocartesian property in affinoid rings.

Case (a): choose a presentation C = A⟨T⟩_M/I, the finite set L, and the compatible system B⟨T⟩_{φ(M)∪L^m}/J_m with J_m the closure of the ideal generated by the image of I; show t_{m_1,m_2} is an open embedding onto a rational subset; take the inductive limit W of the W_m.
Verify the universal property for affinoid test objects V = Spa D via the uniqueness clause of [Hu, 3.5] and factorisation through B⟨T⟩/J_m for m large.
Corollary 1.2.3 (i)-(iii) are read off from the construction; (iii.d) is quoted from the proof of [Hu, 3.9.i].
acceptance: For Z analytic every morphism is adic, so fibre products exist whenever f is locally of weakly finite type.
The affinoid product in case (b) has D^+ equal to the integral closure of C^+ ⊗ B^+, not C^+ ⊗ B^+ itself.
In case (a) the fibre product need not be affinoid when B has topologically nilpotent elements not adjusted by L; it is a union of the affinoid W_m.

nodes.title: Closed adic subspaces, closed/open/locally closed embeddings, and comparison with rigid closed immersions
nodes.statement: For an affinoid ring A = (A^▷, A^+) and an ideal J of A^▷, A/J denotes the affinoid ring (A^▷/J, (A^+/J ∩ A^+)^c) with the quotient topology and the integral closure of A^+/(J∩A^+). For an adic space X and a quasi-coherent ideal I ⊆ O_X, the triple Y = ({x : I_x ≠ O_{X,x}}, (O_X/I)|Y, induced valuations) with the unique ring topology making O_X(U) -> O_Y(Y∩U) continuous and open for affinoid U is an adic space, the closed adic subspace defined by I; for X = Spa A and J = Γ(X,I) it is Spa(A/J). A morphism is a closed (resp. open, locally closed) embedding if it factors as an isomorphism onto such a subspace followed by the inclusion. For a Tate ring A of topologically finite type over a complete non-archimedean field k and any ideal J, (A,A°)/J = (A/J,(A/J)°) [BGR 6.3.4 Prop. 1], hence a morphism of rigid varieties is a closed embedding iff r(f) is a closed embedding of adic spaces.
hypotheses: I is a quasi-coherent O_X-module (the source uses this word; for the affinoid case J is an arbitrary ideal of A^▷)
Existence of the adic space structure on Y is quoted from [Hu4, 3.6] and Huber's unpublished 'Coherent sheaves on adic spaces' [Hu2]; not read
proofSteps: Define A/J with the quotient topology and integrally closed plus-ring; define Y by support of O_X/I; quote [Hu4, 3.6] for the adic-space property.
For the rigid comparison use that quotients of tft Tate algebras have power-bounded elements equal to the image of the integral closure ([BGR 6.3.4 Prop. 1]).
acceptance: Spa(A/J) is a closed adic subspace of Spa A with the ringed-space structure (A^▷/J, integral closure), not merely the closed subset V(J).
Closed embeddings are finite morphisms (Lemma 1.4.5.iii).

nodes.title: Separated, proper and partially proper morphisms; valuative criteria for analytic adic spaces
nodes.statement: Definitions (1.3.1-1.3.3): f is separated if it is locally of weakly finite type and the diagonal has closed image in X ×_Y X; universally closed if locally of weakly finite type and closed after every adic base change; proper if of +weakly finite type, separated and universally closed; (universally) specializing at a point via lifting of specializations (after adic base change); partially proper if locally of +weakly finite type, separated and universally specializing. Lemma 1.3.4: proper iff partially proper and quasi-compact (a quasi-compact specializing morphism is closed because images of closed sets are pro-constructible). Valuative criteria for analytic adic spaces in terms of valuation rings (x,A) of X, A ⊆ k(x)^+, and their centers: Proposition 1.3.7 (f quasi-separated and locally of weakly finite type): separated iff every (x,A) has at most one center over a given point of Y; Proposition 1.3.8: universally specializing at x_0 iff every center of f_v(x_0,A) on Y lifts to a center on X; Corollary 1.3.9: partially proper (resp. proper) iff existence and uniqueness of centers, for f quasi-separated locally of +weakly finite type (resp. of +weakly finite type); Lemma 1.3.10 restates this via diagrams with spectra of affinoid fields. Lemma 1.3.12: for X quasi-compact quasi-separated analytic, the space X_v of valuation rings with the topology generated by D(U,f) is spectral. Lemma 1.3.13: for f partially proper with Y qcqs, closures of quasi-compact subsets of X are quasi-compact. Lemmas 1.3.14-1.3.16: extension/uniqueness lemmas for morphisms defined on dense-generalising opens, injective quasi-compact maps are homeomorphisms onto their image, and specializations of a point with dense residue field are separated by f.
hypotheses: Valuative criteria are stated for analytic adic spaces only ('For simplicity we explain here this criterion only for morphisms between analytic adic spaces'); the general criterion is in [Hu4]
Quasi-separatedness of f is required in 1.3.7 and 1.3.9; +weakly finite type in 1.3.9

Prove 1.3.6: existence/uniqueness of a valuation ring with given support and center, from (1.1.10.iii); a valuation ring has a center on an affinoid X iff f(x) ∈ A for all f ∈ O_X^+(X).

1.3.8: (a)=>(b) via base change to Y' = Spa(k(x),A) and the closed points of X'' = Spa(k(x),k(x)^+); (b)=>(a) by constructing a valuation ring A' ⊆ k(x_0')^+ inducing k(y')^+ and using 1.3.6.ii.

nodes.title: Finite morphisms of adic spaces: definition, base change, properness, and finiteness from proper fibres
nodes.statement: (1.4.2) A morphism of complete affinoid rings A -> B is finite if it is of topologically finite type and A^▷ -> B^▷, A^+ -> B^+ are integral; then B^▷ carries the natural A^▷-module topology and B^+ is the integral closure of A^+; conversely a finite A^▷-algebra with its module topology and the integral closure of A^+ is a complete affinoid ring finite over A [Hu4, 3.12.10]. Lemma 1.4.3 (A, B complete Tate, B = A⟨T⟩/quotient with t_i ∈ B^+): B finite over A iff each t_i satisfies a monic p_i ∈ A^+[X] with p_i(t_i) topologically nilpotent. (1.4.4) f: X -> Y is finite if every y has an affinoid neighbourhood V with f^{-1}(V) affinoid and finite over V; then this holds for every affinoid V [Hu4, 3.6.20, 3.12.12]. Lemma 1.4.5: finite is stable under base change (affinoid product with the module topology), finite implies proper (specializing via [HK, 2.1.2, 2.1.6], trivially via 1.3.9 over analytic bases), closed embeddings are finite, and a rigid morphism is finite iff r(f) is finite. Proposition 1.4.6/Lemma 1.4.7: for f: X -> Y of finite type between analytic affinoid adic spaces, if the fibre X ×_Y Spa κ(y) is proper over Spa κ(y) then f is finite over an open neighbourhood of y; in particular proper implies finite. Lemma 1.4.8: topological nilpotence of an element b in the completed fibre B ⊗̂_A k(x) spreads to a rational neighbourhood of x. Lemma 1.4.9: finiteness descends along a finite h: T' -> T with O(T') faithfully flat over O(T).

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms and the finiteness theorem 'quasi-finite and proper equals finite'
nodes.statement: Definition 1.5.1: f locally quasi-finite if locally of weakly finite type with discrete fibres; quasi-finite if moreover quasi-compact. Lemma 1.5.2 (f weakly of finite type between analytic adic spaces): quasi-finite iff all fibres finite iff fibres over maximal points finite iff k(x)^^ finite over k(f(x))^^ for all x (resp. all maximal x) iff X ×_Y Spa κ(y) -> Spa κ(y) is finite for all maximal y; (a),(b),(d) are equivalent without analyticity. Corollary 1.5.3: locally quasi-finite is stable under base change (f locally of finite type, or g adic) and fibre-product points surject onto compatible pairs. Proposition 1.5.4: for f locally of weakly finite type between analytic adic spaces, locally quasi-finite iff O_{X,x} is finite over O_{Y,f(x)} at maximal points x; if f is locally of finite type also iff f is finite on a neighbourhood of each maximal point. Proposition 1.5.5: for f locally of finite type between analytic adic spaces, f is quasi-finite and proper iff f is finite. Proposition 1.5.6 (f locally of finite type, X quasi-separated, Y qcqs): locally quasi-finite and partially proper iff each x has opens U ⊇ closure{x}, V ⊇ closure{f(x)} with f: U -> V finite. Proposition 1.5.7 / Lemma 1.5.9: for rigid f, locally quasi-finite (dim f^{-1}(y) ≤ 0) iff r(f) locally quasi-finite; and for such f, partially proper (Kiehl-type relative compactness of affinoid pieces) iff r(f) partially proper, with no discreteness assumption on the valuation. Lemma 1.5.10: for a maximal point x of an affinoid Tate space, closure{x} is the intersection of the rational subsets containing it and of their closures.
hypotheses: Analytic adic spaces throughout 1.5.2 (except the equivalences (a),(b),(d)), 1.5.4-1.5.6
1.5.5: f locally of finite type between analytic adic spaces; properness in the sense of 1.3.2
1.5.2 uses Noether normalisation and integrality of the power-bounded subring for tft Tate algebras over an affinoid field ([BGR 6.1.2 Cor. 2, 6.3.4 Prop. 1])

1.5.4: for B of topologically finite type over A use 1.5.2(f) and 1.4.7 to get finiteness near a maximal point and identify O_{Y,y_0} ⊗ O_X(f^{-1}V) with the product of the stalks over y_0; for the +weakly case pass through Z = Spa(B^▷,(B^▷)°).

nodes.title: Universal derivations, Omega_{X/Y}, and the infinitesimal definitions of unramified, smooth and etale morphisms
nodes.statement: For complete f-adic rings A -> B of topologically finite type, a universal continuous A-derivation d_{B/A}: B -> Ω_{B/A} into a complete topological B-module exists (1.6.2): (i) from a presentation B = A⟨X_1..X_n⟩_{M}/I it is the quotient of the free module on dX_i by the submodule generated by I·Ω and d(P) for generators P of I, so Ω_{B/A} is finitely generated and free with basis dX_i when I = 0; (ii) Ω_{B/A} = I/I^2 for the kernel I of B ⊗̂_A B -> B, which is a finitely generated ideal; (iii) if B is finite over A it is the algebraic universal derivation. Proposition 1.6.3: first fundamental exact sequence, conormal sequence for open surjections B -> C, base change along adic A -> A', and compatibility with localisations B(T/s). For f: X -> Y locally of weakly finite type, Ω_{X/Y} := Δ^*(I) for the ideal I of the diagonal in X ×_Y X; on affinoid pieces it is the module associated with Ω_{O_X(U)/O_Y(V)}. Lemma 1.6.4: for f locally quasi-finite between analytic adic spaces, at maximal points the stalk O_{X,x} is finite over O_{Y,f(x)} and the induced derivation is universal; a flat locally quasi-finite morphism stays flat after arbitrary base change. Definition 1.6.5: f is unramified (resp. smooth, etale) if locally of finite type (resp. finite presentation, finite presentation) and Hom_Y(Spa A, X) -> Hom_Y(Spa A/I, X) is injective (resp. surjective, bijective) for every affinoid ring A and square-zero ideal I of A^▷. Example 1.6.6: over discrete bases these agree with the scheme notions; over noetherian complete f-adic A the finite etale adic spaces over Spa(A,A^+) correspond to finite etale schemes over Spec A. Propositions 1.6.7-1.6.9 (stated, 'can be proved similarly as for schemes'): open embeddings are etale, locally closed embeddings unramified, Spa A⟨X⟩_T -> Spa A is smooth; composition, base change, cancellation, and locality on the source; unramified iff Ω_{X/Y} = 0 iff the diagonal is an open embedding iff locally a closed embedding into an etale Y-space; for smooth X -> Y, Ω is locally free, closed subspaces are etale/smooth at x iff generators of the ideal have differentials forming (part of) a basis, and a Y-morphism between spaces locally of finite type is etale/smooth iff d on Ω is bijective / left-invertible. Corollary 1.6.10: f: X -> Spa A is smooth iff locally it factors as an etale map to Spa A⟨T_1..T_n⟩_{M}; if A is Tate one can take all M_i = {1}.

nodes.statement: Proposition 1.7.1: for an affinoid ring A (not necessarily complete) and s: X -> Y = Spa A between affinoid adic spaces, s is etale iff X ≅ Spa B/I with B = A⟨X_1..X_n⟩_{T_1..T_n}, I = (f_1..f_n) and det(∂f_i/∂X_j) a unit in B^▷/I, where the f_i may be taken in B^▷ (ii) or even in A^▷[X_1..X_n] (iii). Corollary 1.7.2: the presentation is stable under small perturbation of the f_i (isomorphic quotient with e^*(x̄_i) close to x̄_i), and over a Tate A one may take all T_i = {1}. Corollary 1.7.3: for a ring homomorphism φ: D -> A^▷, every scheme X locally of finite type over Spec D defines X^ad := X ×_{Spec D} Spa A locally of finite type over Spa A ([Hu, 3.8]); (i) etale X -> Spec D gives etale X^ad -> Spa A; (ii) if im φ is dense, every affinoid etale Y -> Spa A is an open subspace of X^ad for some affine etale X -> Spec D; (iii) Y -> Spa A is etale iff Y ≅ Spa B with A -> B of algebraically finite type and A^▷ -> B^▷ algebraically etale. Corollary 1.7.4: unramified implies locally quasi-finite. Proposition 1.7.5 (f locally of finite type between analytic adic spaces): etale iff flat and unramified iff at maximal points O_{X,x} is flat over O_{Y,f(x)} with fibre a finite separable extension of k(f(x)). Lemma 1.7.6: etale between affinoid adic spaces implies O_Y(Y) -> O_X(X) flat (proved when A^▷ has a noetherian ring of definition, and when A^▷ is a strongly noetherian Tate ring). nodes.title: The functor r from rigid analytic varieties to adic spaces and its equivalence onto quasi-separated locally finite type spaces
nodes.statement: For a complete non-archimedean field k there is a functor r = r_k from rigid analytic varieties over Sp k to adic spaces over Spa(k,k°) ([Hu, 4.3]) characterised by: (a) r(Sp A) = Spa(A, A°) with r(f) induced by the k-algebra map; (b) open embeddings go to open embeddings; (c) a family of admissible opens is an admissible covering iff the r(X_i) cover r(X); (d) r is fully faithful. r(X) is locally of finite type over Spa(k,k°); r restricts to an equivalence between quasi-separated rigid varieties over Sp k (more generally over any rigid X) and adic spaces over Spa(k,k°) (over r(X)) whose structure morphisms are locally of finite type and quasi-separated. The points of X are identified with the points x of r(X) whose residue field k(x) is finite over k; admissible opens U satisfy r(U) ∩ X = U; for quasi-separated X, quasi-compact admissible opens correspond bijectively to quasi-compact opens of r(X) (affinoids to affinoids); constructible subsets of r(X) are determined by their trace on X; r commutes with fibre products; and the morphism of sites r(X) -> X induces an equivalence of topoi.

nodes.statement: A formal scheme X = (X, O_X) is of type (S) if every point has an open affine neighbourhood U such that the topology of A := O_X(U) is adic and either (a) A is noetherian, or (b) there is s ∈ A with sA an ideal of definition and the Tate ring A(1/s) (the localisation A_s topologised by {im(s^n A -> A_s)}) strongly noetherian. (1.9.5) Let f: X -> Y be locally of finite type between schemes, Y' ⊆ Y closed defined by a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, X' = X ×_Y Y', and X̂, Ŷ the completions; if Ŷ is of type (S) then so is X̂, f̂ is adic, and the commutative square of σ's induces a d(Ŷ)-morphism φ: d(X̂) -> X ×_Y d(Ŷ) into the fibre product of [Hu, 3.8]. Proposition 1.9.6: (i) φ is a local isomorphism; (ii) if f is separated, φ is injective; (iii) if f is universally specializing, φ is surjective; hence for f separated and universally specializing (e.g. proper), φ is an isomorphism. nodes.title: Conrad's Berthelot-type functor (·)^rig on FS_C for non-discretely valued k, and its preserved properties
nodes.statement: Fix an adic noetherian ring C with a continuous map C -> R to the valuation ring R of a complete non-archimedean field k (Examples: C = R when k is discretely valued; in general a complete DVR R_0 ⊆ R with R_0 -> R local; or C = Z discrete). FS_C is the category of locally noetherian formal schemes over Spf C whose underlying reduced scheme is locally of finite type over C_red; affine opens have algebras that are quotients of (C[[q_1..q_n]]){{T_1..T_m}}. For X in FS_C and a rigid space X over k, Hom^cont_C(X, X) consists of morphisms of locally ringed G-topologised spaces whose ring maps are C-algebra maps landing in locally power-bounded sections and carrying locally topologically nilpotent sections to such. Theorem 3.1.5: Hom^cont_C(·, X) is represented by a quasi-separated rigid space X^rig; (·)^rig takes open/closed immersions to open/closed immersions and open covers to admissible covers, commutes with fibre products (a), with analytic extension of k (b) and with change of C (c), preserves separatedness (d), and sends topologically finite type maps to quasi-compact maps (e). Theorem 3.1.6 (statement; proof only partially read): for f locally topologically of finite type, (·)^rig preserves finiteness, formal smoothness of pure relative dimension d (formally etale to etale), finite flatness of constant rank, properness, (faithful) flatness, fibre-dimension bounds, and flatness with geometrically reduced fibres of pure dimension d.
hypotheses: C adic noetherian with continuous C -> R; k arbitrary complete non-archimedean (no discreteness)
Objects of FS_C are locally noetherian formal schemes; this functor does not apply to non-noetherian formal O_K-models when k is not discretely valued (those are the Bosch-Lutkebohmert setting)
Theorem 3.1.6 proof: only its first paragraph was read
proofSteps: Δ -> Spf C[[q]] pulling q back to the disc coordinate serves as Spf(C[[q]])^rig, because topologically nilpotent elements of a k-affinoid have sup norm < 1 and Δ is covered by the discs Δ_r.
For X = Spf(C[[q]]{{T}}/J) take the zero locus of J in Δ^n × B^m; identify (Spf A_{a})^rig with the locus where a is a unit with power-bounded inverse via A_{a} ≅ A{{T}}/(1 - aT).
Glue over open covers, first for separated X then in general; deduce (a)-(e).
acceptance: For C = Z[[q^{1/n}]] and the formal Tate curve, (·)^rig produces the relative Tate curve over the open unit disc (the source's application in §3.1, not read).
When k is discretely valued and C = R the functor recovers de Jong's [deJ, 7.2.4, 7.2.6].

nodes.title: Admissibility of the Hasse-invariant loci S^{>h}, S^{≥h} via a formal model and a local formal-group coefficient (Conrad 4.1.1)
nodes.statement: For a generalized elliptic curve E -> S over a rigid space S over k, the loci S^{>h} (h ∈ [1/p,1) ∩ sqrt|k^×|) and S^{≥h} (h ∈ (1/p,1] ∩ sqrt|k^×|) of points whose fibre has Hasse invariant > h (resp. ≥ h) are admissible opens, their formation commutes with base change on S and with analytic extension of k, S^{≥h} -> S is quasi-compact, and {S^{≥h}}_{h > h_0} is an admissible cover of S^{>h_0}. Proof route read: by fpqc descent of admissible opens and of the properties 'open immersion' and 'quasi-compact' ([C3, 4.2.4, 4.2.7]) reduce to the universal Γ_1(N)-structure over the proper finitely presented R-scheme M (Theorem 3.2.3 for the analytified moduli interpretation); properness gives Ê^rig ≅ E^an_k and M̂^rig ≅ M^an_k ([C1, 5.3.1(4)]); on a formal affine Spf A ⊆ M̂ where e^*Ω̂^1 is trivial, the formal completion Γ_A of Ê along the identity is Spf(A[[X]]) with a formal group law, and with a_{Γ_A} the coefficient of X^p in [p]^*(X) the loci |a_{Γ_A}| > h (resp. ≥ h) on (Spf A)^rig are independent of the coordinate; by Lemma A.1.5 every point s of M^an_k is s^rig for a map A -> R_0 into the valuation ring of a finite extension, E_s has semistable reduction with formal group the completion of Ê_s, so h(E_s) = max(1/p, |a_{Γ_A}(s)|) by Definition B.3.3; hence S^{>h} ∩ (Spf A)^rig = {|a_{Γ_A}| > h}. The Hasse invariant here is h(E_k) = max(|a|,1/p) for a lifting the X^p-coefficient of [p] modulo p on the formal group of a semistable model (B.3.3), not a section of a line bundle.
hypotheses: k a complete non-archimedean field with valuation ring R, p the residue characteristic; h constrained to sqrt|k^×| in the stated ranges

E -> S a generalized elliptic curve over a rigid space; the reduction to a proper finitely presented R-scheme M uses Theorem 3.2.3 (analytified moduli) and Corollary 2.2.5 / Theorems 2.2.3-2.2.4, 3.2.1 (not read)
Ê^rig ≅ E^an_k requires properness over R ([C1, 5.3.1(4)], unread)
Lemma A.1.5 (rig-points) is imported from Bosch-Lutkebohmert I §3.5 (unread)

Trivialise e^*Ω̂^1 on formal affines and write the formal group as Spf A[[X]].
Show the coordinate-independence of |a_{Γ_A}| > h for h in the stated range.
Use rig-points (A.1.5) to compute h(E_s) fibrewise and identify the loci.

nodes.title: Conrad's fibral finiteness criterion for flat rigid maps (A.1.2) with its scheme lemma (A.1.4) and formal-model imports
nodes.statement: Theorem A.1.2: a flat map f: X -> Y of rigid spaces over k (no discreteness assumption) is finite iff it is quasi-compact and separated with finite fibres and locally constant fibre rank on Y. Lemma A.1.4: a flat, locally finitely presented morphism of schemes is finite iff it is separated with finite fibres and locally constant fibre rank (no quasi-compactness needed). Lemma A.1.5: for Y flat and locally topologically of finite presentation over Spf R, every point y: Sp(k') -> Y^rig is y^rig for a unique closed immersion Spf B -> Y with B a finite flat R-domain, and every closed point of Y underlies such a map ([BL1, 3.5]). Remark A.1.3: the discretely valued case is Abbes-Mokrane [AM, Lemme A.1] (whose 'quasi-separated' must be strengthened to 'separated'); their completion argument fails for nondiscrete k since local rings of formal models are then non-noetherian. Proof of A.1.2 as read: reduce to Y affinoid, X, Y quasi-compact separated, constant rank d; choose a formal model f: X -> Y, automatically separated ([BL1, Prop. 4.7]), quasi-finite after modification ([BL2, Cor. 5.3]) and flat after further modification ([BL2, Thm. 5.2]) since base change and closed formal subschemes preserve quasi-finiteness and separatedness; it suffices that f_n = f mod I^{n+1} are finite, and each f_n is quasi-finite, separated, flat, finitely presented, so by A.1.4 it suffices that the fibres of the special-fibre map f̄ have constant rank d; constructibility ([EGA IV_3, 9.8.8]) reduces to closed points y_0; by A.1.5 pick Spf B -> Y through y_0 with B finite flat local; T = X ×_Y Spf B is quasi-finite flat over Spf B with one-point special fibre, hence affine and finite, T = Spf C with C finite free of rank d' over B; C ⊗_R k is the affinoid algebra of f^{-1}(y_k) of rank d, so d' = d. Proof of A.1.4 as read: reduce to constant rank d; for local Y base change fpqc to a henselian local ring, split X = X' ⊔ X'' by [EGA IV_4, 18.5.11(c)] with X' finite over Y and X'' with empty closed fibre, deduce X' finite free of rank d' = d and X' = X; for general Y spread out from Spec O_{Y,y} using a quasi-compact open U ⊇ X ×_Y Spec O_{Y,y} and finite presentation.
hypotheses: f flat; quasi-compact; separated (quasi-separated is insufficient, cf. Remark A.1.3); finite fibres; fibre rank locally constant on Y
k arbitrary complete non-archimedean field; formal models over Spf R with R possibly non-noetherian

Imported and unread: [BL1, Prop. 4.7] (separatedness of formal models of separated rigid maps), [BL1, §3.5] (rig-points), [BL2, Thm. 5.2] (flattening by admissible blow-up), [BL2, Cor. 5.3] (quasi-finite formal models), [EGA IV_4, 18.5.11(c)], [EGA IV_3, 9.8.8], [EGA IV_2 for finite presentation spreading]
Necessity of quasi-compactness: the bijective local isomorphism {|t| = 1} ⊔ {|t| < 1} -> {|t| ≤ 1}
proofSteps: Scheme lemma A.1.4 via henselian base change, the structure theorem for separated locally quasi-finite maps, constancy of rank over the closed fibre and spreading out.
Formal-model reductions: separated, quasi-finite and flat models by [BL1]/[BL2].
Reduce finiteness of the formal map to finiteness of each f_n, then to constant fibre rank of the special fibre by A.1.4.
Compute the rank at closed points through rig-points and the finite free algebra C over the local finite flat domain B.
acceptance: A finite flat rigid map has locally constant fibre rank, and conversely under the stated hypotheses.

The criterion is not a consequence of Huber 1.5.5 as stated: 1.5.5 needs properness (universal closedness), whereas A.1.2 replaces it by flatness plus locally constant rank; conversely A.1.2's conclusion implies properness.
Over a discretely valued k the statement is Abbes-Mokrane Lemme A.1 with 'separated'.

nodes.title: Topological invariance of affinoidness and finiteness (Conrad A.1.1)
nodes.statement: A rigid space X is affinoid iff X_red is affinoid; hence a morphism of rigid spaces is finite iff the induced morphism of reduced spaces is finite. Proof as read: i: Y_red -> Y induces a 'homeomorphism' of G-topologies (admissible opens and coverings lift uniquely), by reduction to affinoids and the Gerritzen-Grauert description of affinoid subdomains through rational and Weierstrass domains [BGR 7.3.5/3]; hence X is quasi-compact quasi-separated when X_red is affinoid and the nilpotent coherent ideal I allows induction to the square-zero case X_0 = Sp(A_0) ⊂ X; then A = O_X(X) is a k-Banach algebra of countable type via the left exact sequence over a finite affinoid cover, the extension 0 -> I -> A -> A_0 -> 0 with I a finite A_0-module, power-bounded lifts a_r of topological generators exist because power-boundedness is insensitive to nilpotents, [BGR 6.1.1/4] gives k⟨t,u⟩ -> A surjective, and the map ι: X -> Sp(A) is a closed immersion by [BGR 9.5.3/5], hence an isomorphism. The source notes that a Serre-type cohomological criterion for affinoidness is unavailable ([Liu] gives a qcqs surface with vanishing higher coherent cohomology that is not affinoid).
hypotheses: Rigid spaces over a complete non-archimedean field k; no discreteness
Inputs from BGR (6.1.1/4, 7.3.5/3, 9.5.3/5) were not read
proofSteps: G-topology invariance under nil-thickening; reduction to square-zero ideals; Banach-algebra structure on global sections; lifting generators; closed-immersion criterion.
acceptance: A finite morphism can be recognised on reduced spaces; Conrad uses this together with A.1.2 in the canonical subgroup construction.

nodes.title: Tate acyclicity and Kiehl's coherent-sheaf equivalence for adic affinoid algebras over an analytic field (Kedlaya-Liu 2.5.20)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A^+) be an adic Banach ring with A an affinoid algebra over an analytic field K (A^+ = A° not assumed). A is noetherian, every ideal is closed, finite A-modules are canonically finite Banach modules with continuous strict maps (2.5.2); Noether normalisation K{T_1..T_n} -> A finite strict (2.5.4); maximal ideals have residue fields finite over K and Maxspec(A) embeds in M(A) and in Spa(A,A^+) (2.5.5). Theorem 2.5.20: for an affinoid covering U of Spa(A,A^+) and a finite A-module M with associated O-module M̃, the Čech cohomology Ȟ^i(Spa(A,A^+), M̃; U) is M for i = 0 and 0 for i > 0 (in particular (A,A^+) is sheafy and H^i(Spa, M̃) = M, 0), and M -> M̃ is a tensor equivalence between finite A-modules and coherent O-modules; equivalently A -> B_1 ⊕ ... ⊕ B_n is an effective descent morphism for finite Banach modules. Corollary 2.5.21: closed-open subsets correspond to idempotents. The proofs are citations of Tate [BGR 8.2.1/5] and Kiehl [BGR 9.4.3/3].
hypotheses: A an affinoid algebra over an analytic field K (Hypothesis 2.5.1); A^+ arbitrary ring of integral elements
The Tate and Kiehl proofs live in BGR, not in the library; only the reduction to the adic spectrum was read
proofSteps: Import Tate's acyclicity and Kiehl's theorem from BGR; KL check that the adic-spectrum formulation follows from the classical Maxspec statements via 2.5.9-2.5.19 (rational subdomains, Lemma 2.5.10 refinement of Maxspec coverings, Prop. 2.5.18 sheafiness).

nodes.title: Acyclicity of the structure sheaf and Kiehl gluing of finite projective modules over sheafy adic Banach rings (Kedlaya-Liu 2.4.23, 2.7.7)
nodes.statement: Theorem 2.4.23: if (A,A^+) is sheafy then for every rational covering U of Spa(A,A^+), H^i(Spa, O) = Ȟ^i(Spa, O; U) equals A for i = 0 and 0 for i > 0; proof reduces by Proposition 2.4.21 to simple Laurent coverings, for which 0 -> A -> B_1 ⊕ B_2 -> B_{12} -> 0 is exact at B_{12} (Lemma 2.4.22) and, by sheafiness, at A and B_1 ⊕ B_2. Glueing squares (Definition 2.7.3): a commutative square R -> R_1, R_2 -> R_{12} of Banach rings with 0 -> R -> R_1 ⊕ R_2 -> R_{12} -> 0 strict exact, R_2 -> R_{12} of dense image, and M(R_1 ⊕ R_2) -> M(R) surjective. Lemma 2.7.2: for a strict surjection ψ: R_1 ⊕ R_2 -> S there is c > 0 such that every U ∈ GL_n(S) with |U - 1| < c factors as ψ(U_1)ψ(U_2). Lemma 2.7.4 / Proposition 2.7.5: for a finite projective glueing datum (M_1, M_2, M_{12}) on a glueing square, the kernel M of M_1 ⊕ M_2 -> M_{12} is a finite projective R-module with M ⊗_R R_i ≅ M_i. Definition 2.7.6 / Theorem 2.7.7: for sheafy (A,A^+) the structure sheaf satisfies the Tate sheaf property (acyclicity on every rational localisation) and the Kiehl glueing property (finite projective O(U)-modules ≅ locally free O-modules of finite rank on every rational U). Remark 2.7.1: rational localisation need not be flat in general (fails for perfectoid algebras), which is why only finite projective modules are glued.
hypotheses: (A,A^+) sheafy (structure presheaf is a sheaf on every rational subspace)
Kiehl glueing is proved only for finite projective (locally free of finite rank) modules, not for all finite modules
proofSteps: Prove Čech acyclicity for simple Laurent coverings and reduce general rational coverings to them (Propositions 2.4.20-2.4.21).
Matrix factorisation (2.7.2) by successive approximation with constant d^{-2}.
Glue generators (2.7.4) by correcting the transition matrix with C_1 C_2^{-1}; conclude projectivity via Lemma 1.3.9 and surjectivity of Spec(R_1 ⊕ R_2) -> Spec R on maximal ideals through M(R).
Assemble 2.7.7 from acyclicity, 2.4.20 and 2.7.5.

For a perfectoid affinoid, rational localisation is not flat, so gluing of arbitrary finite modules is not asserted.

nodes.title: Stably uniform adic Banach rings are sheafy (Buzzard-Verberkmoes, Kedlaya-Liu 2.8.10) and the splitting criterion
nodes.statement: A uniform Banach ring has norm equivalent to a power-multiplicative one (Definition 2.8.1); (A,A^+) is stably uniform if every rational localisation is uniform. Theorem 2.8.10: a stably uniform adic Banach ring is sheafy (proof: Corollary 2.8.9 verifies the criterion of Proposition 2.4.21 for simple Laurent coverings). Remark 2.8.11: whether every sheafy uniform ring is stably uniform is open; a sheafy ring with a rational covering by stably uniform rings is stably uniform. Remark 2.8.12: if A -> B is a bounded morphism of adic Banach rings with B stably uniform and A -> B split in Banach A-modules, then A is stably uniform (the splitting persists under rational localisation, and uniformity follows from criterion (c) of 2.8.1).

nodes.title: The etale site of an adic space and the equivalence with the rigid etale topos (Huber 2.1)
nodes.statement: The etale site X_et of an adic space X is Et/X (adic spaces etale over X) with coverings the families (U_i -> U) whose images cover U (surjective families); this is a site by 1.6.7 and 1.2.3.iii.d, and f: X -> Y induces a morphism of sites via base change (1.5.3.ii, 1.7.4). Definition 2.1.1: an etale morphism of rigid varieties is strongly surjective if every quasi-compact admissible open of the target is the image of finitely many quasi-compact admissible opens of the source; the rigid etale site uses strongly surjective families ([SS, §1]). Lemma 2.1.2: f strongly surjective iff r(f) surjective (via pro-constructibility of images of quasi-compact opens under the spectral maps f_i, determination of constructible sets by rigid points, and openness of etale maps 1.7.8/1.7.11). (2.1.3): r commutes with the site morphisms. Proposition 2.1.4: ρ_X: r(X)~_et -> X~_et is an equivalence of topoi; proof: r is an equivalence between the quasi-separated subsites X'_et and r(X)'_et (by 1.1.11, 1.7.11, 2.1.2), every object has a covering by quasi-separated objects, so the comparison lemma [SGA 4, III.4.1] applies. (2.2.1)-(2.2.2): locally constant functions form a sheaf; Hom_X(-, Z) is a sheaf on X_et if Z is etale over X (proof read: descent of a morphism with h∘p_1 = h∘p_2 through the image U, Zariski's main theorem giving Z open in a finite T, and the finite etale A -> B being bijective by comparing maximal ideals via [Hu, 1.4]) or if X is analytic (proof via a criterion (1) with open and finite-etale coverings, not read).
hypotheses: Etale morphisms as in 1.6.5; coverings by surjective families
2.1.4 is a statement about topoi of sheaves of sets on the two sites; the site morphism uses the quasi-separated subsites
2.2.2(b) (X analytic) relies on Lemma 2.2.8 and [JP, 3.2.2], not read

Prove 2.1.4 by the comparison lemma on quasi-separated subsites.
2.2.2(a): reduce to X, Z affinoid, show U = h(Y) is closed and open in a finite T, and that O_T(U) ≅ O_X(X).

nodes.title: Sousperfectoid Tate rings: stability under rational localisation, finite etale extension and Tate algebras, and sheafiness (Scholze-Weinstein 6.3, after Hansen-Kedlaya)
nodes.statement: Definition 6.3.1: a complete Tate Z_p-algebra R is sousperfectoid if there is a perfectoid Tate ring R̃ with an injection R -> R̃ that splits as topological R-modules.
